title: German youth movement stages nationwide protests over living costs and education
seoTitle: Berlin youth protests over living costs

tea.why: Youth are protesting to address high living costs, underfunded schools, environmental issues, and potential mandatory military service.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand attention to youth priorities including living costs, increased education spending, and solutions for housing deficits.
tea.changed: Nov 2: Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for tough action against rioters while acknowledging legitimate youth concerns.

summary: Tens of thousands of young people participated in nationwide demonstrations organized by the movement "Gen Z regelt!" across German cities including Berlin, Frankfurt, Cologne, and Hamburg. The protests coincided with Halloween to maximize visibility and focused on issues such as the high cost of living, underfunded schools, environmental concerns, and potential mandatory military service. While the majority of participants demonstrated peacefully, unrest and clashes with police occurred on the sidelines in several locations, involving property damage, looting, and attacks on emergency personnel. Politicians responded by condemning the violence and pledging a hard stance against troublemakers, while also acknowledging the legitimacy of the youth's core demands.
response: Police deployed water cannons, riot guards, and extra personnel, resulting in dozens of investigations and some arrests. Chancellor Friedrich Merz and other officials condemned the violence, promising strict legal action against rioters while acknowledging the legitimate concerns of peaceful protesters.

arrests.text: investigations are underway against 54 people in Frankfurt, with an 18-year-old placed in pre-trial detention

injuries.text: More than 100 police officers were injured

updates.text: Tens of thousands turned out across Germany for youth-led demonstrations organized by "Gen Z regelt!" coinciding with Halloween.
Clashes, looting, and attacks on police occurred on the margins of the demonstrations in cities like Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne, and Hamburg.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz demanded strict legal action against rioters while recognizing the validity of the youth's underlying concerns.
